hook: The *$1 billion* reason offices might be empty Nov. 19
dek: Workers are using PTO and sick days to play Grand Theft Auto VI on day one.

slides.label: What happened
slides.text: Grand Theft Auto VI drops *November 19* on PS5 and Xbox, and offices are bracing for empty seats.

slides.label: The numbers
slides.text: A survey of 1,000 gamers found *39%* plan PTO, *36%* will call in sick, and *32%* will fake WFH that day.

slides.label: Why the hype
slides.text: It's been *13 years* since the last main GTA game, and critics call this the decade's most anticipated release.

slides.label: One worker's plan
slides.text: Jake, a tech PR worker, told his manager he's taking a 4 day weekend. She said, 'use your PTO how you want.'

slides.label: The price tag
slides.text: A Spanish economist estimates the launch could cost the U.S. *$1 billion* in lost productivity.

slides.label: Companies respond
slides.text: Burger Motorsports, a California auto company, announced a company-wide pause for 'this unprecedented cultural event.'

slides.label: Mixed signals
slides.text: 33% expect their boss to be supportive, but 12.5% say 'not supportive' and over 1 in 5 said, 'they'll never know.'

slides.label: Why it matters
slides.text: For workers without flexible jobs or paid leave, the same break from work often isn't an option at all.

question: PTO, sick day, or fake WFH for GTA VI? Pick one.
first_comment: One Berkeley engineer is playing in memory of his wife who passed before launch. A quiet, heavy moment amid all the hype.
photo_caption: Grand Theft Auto VI launches November 19 on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S.
caption_instagram:
Grand Theft Auto VI drops November 19, and workers across the country are already lining up PTO requests, sick days, and fake 'work from home' days just to play it, according to Fast Company.

A new GameSquare and Pollfish survey of 1,000 gamers found 39% are requesting time off in advance, 36% plan to call in sick, and 32% say they'll fake working from home. A Spanish economist estimates the launch could cost the U.S. a full $1 billion in lost productivity, and companies like Burger Motorsports are literally pausing operations for release day.

It's been 13 years since the last mainline GTA title, and for players like Dustin Hall, who's playing in memory of his late wife, this isn't just a game, it's a moment.

PTO, sick day, or fake WFH for GTA VI? Pick one.

caption_linkedin:
Grand Theft Auto VI launches November 19, and the numbers say a lot about workplace culture right now, not just gaming. A GameSquare and Pollfish survey of 1,000 employed gamers found 39% plan to request PTO in advance, 36% will call in sick, and 32% plan to work from home while actually playing, according to Fast Company.

One Spanish economist estimates the game's release could cost the U.S. $1 billion in lost productivity. Some companies are getting ahead of it. Burger Motorsports announced a company-wide operational pause for release day instead of fighting an unwinnable battle against absenteeism.

For founders and managers, this is less about one video game and more about how people actually use PTO when they don't feel safe asking for it outright. Experts quoted in the piece argue predictable cultural moments, game launches, the Super Bowl Monday, holidays, should be treated as coordination problems, not trust issues.
